claims: alerts/rules/peg-rule-definitions.tftest.hcl:68-69 — the required Terraform test still asserts the old title contract (requires peg_slack_title.template to contain $alert.Annotations.summary and $alert.Annotations.resolved_summary while peg-message-templates.tf:13-15 now renders only a status icon), so CI fails and this blocks the branch outright

ui-dashboard/src/app/api/peg-monitoring/alerts/peg-alert-events.ts:109-110 — a rule that goes Alerting straight out of Error no longer opens an alert cycle (transitionKind classifies previous=Error, current=Alerting as error-recovered-alerting, which pairStateTransitions treats only as closing the :error cycle), so its resolution loses its duration (no 'lasted N min') and evidence falls back to the Normal transition's values, making downsideCause print the recovered measurement as the breach magnitude
route.test.ts:345,395 — neither of the two sequences that break (e.g. Normal→Error→Alerting→Normal) is covered by the test suite, which is why this got through

peg-alert-events.ts:230 — evaluation-failure copy says 'Price source' for rules that have no source; pegAlertSourceName("") returns the literal 'Price source' for Structural Saturation Warning, Indexed Pool Unreachable, Heartbeat Missing and Policy Rollover Stuck, so a Grafana error renders 'Grafana could not evaluate the Price source Peg rule'
docs/notes/peg-monitoring.md:118-119 — 'Slack titles use the severity icon plus that summary' is now false; the title is the icon alone and the linked summary moved to the body

docs/notes/peg-monitoring.md:132-133 — 'The history backend reads only fired and resolved transitions… It does not read Pending or canceled transitions' is now false; it also reads Error, Error→Normal and Error→Alerting
docs/notes/peg-monitoring.md:110-111 — 'The state dot shows whether the condition is active, urgent, or resolved' is now false; recent-alerts.tsx:22-29 adds three monitoring-state labels
route.ts:58-84 — back to four upstream Grafana calls; fetchJson now fans each URL out to two requests under Promise.all, re-introducing the fan-out that commit 56dff428 cut from four to two

route.ts:58-84 — any non-2xx, non-JSON or 8s timeout on the added Error query throws out of Promise.all and the endpoint returns 502, so the Recent-alerts panel goes to 'unavailable' for a query that only ever adds supplementary rows; it should degrade gracefully

Unconfirmed — peg-alert-events.ts:162-171 fails the entire response closed on a single unrecognised row (any row failing stateLineSchema or carrying a values key outside the .strict() whitelist at :22-35 throws InvalidPegAlertsUpstreamError for the whole request), and now sees an Error-state row class whose values payload nobody has validated, which could turn rare evaluation errors into a fully blank panel
New cosmetic issue on Alerting→Error→Normal — the panel now shows a green 'Grafana can evaluate the rule again' row beside a red still-active row
Pre-existing, out of scope — route.ts:102-113 computes policyUrl and only null-checks it; it is never fetched

1.why: peg-rule-definitions.tftest.hcl:68-69 does assert $alert.Annotations.summary/resolved_summary while the new template renders only an icon — this is the known 'Update the stale Terraform title assertion' item

2.why: transitionKind():109-110 returns error-recovered-alerting for previous=Error/current=Alerting; isOpening()/cycleKey() at 318-321 route it to the :error cycle only, so the later cleared row hits unpairedCleared (346/354) and is phrased with raised=undefined — no 'lasted', and evidence falls back to the Normal row, whose values.A downsideCause prints; base transitionKind treated any current=Alerting as raised, so this is a regression

3.why: grepped every previous/current pair in route.test.ts: the two new tests (345, 398) cover Normal→Error→Normal and Alerting→Error→Alerting only; no test exercises Error→Alerting→Normal or Alerting→Error→Normal

4.why: peg-alert-events.ts:230 with pegAlertSourceName('')→'Price source' (peg-alert-copy.ts:47-49) is the known 'Label source-less evaluation failures by rule' item

5.why: docs/notes/peg-monitoring.md:118-119 is the only 'severity icon' text in the repo and is the runbook the known 'Keep the Peg runbook aligned with the new title' item points at

6.why: doc lines 132-133 still say the backend reads only fired and resolved transitions, but route.ts:43-56 now also issues current=Error and previous=Error queries and peg-alert-events.ts:108-111 classifies three new Error kinds; the doc is untouched by the diff

7.why: SEVERITY_COLOR (recent-alerts.tsx:10-14) and the dot itself are unchanged — the dot still shows active/urgent/resolved; only the aria-label text was extended, and the doc already says 'Each dot also has an accessible state label'

8.why: the count is accurate (fetchJson fans each URL to two, tests now assert 4 calls), but 56dff428 cut the calls to drop high-cardinality Pending queries, and the claim names no concrete harm beyond the count

9.why: route.ts:65-82 puts both URLs in one Promise.all with no per-URL catch, so a non-ok/non-JSON Error-query response rejects the whole GET → 502 at 129-132 (timeout → 504), taking down the panel for a supplementary query

10.why: the fail-closed mechanism at 162-171 and the .strict() values whitelist at 22-35 are real, but the claim is self-labelled Unconfirmed and never establishes that Error rows carry values outside the whitelist

11.why: Alerting→Error→Normal closes only the :error cycle and leaves the alert cycle in `open` (emitted at 356), i.e. the known 'peg-alert-events.ts:352 Error recovery leaves breach active'

12.why: policyUrl is indeed only null-checked (route.ts:102/111) and never fetched, but it is identical in base (81/90) — pre-existing and self-declared out of scope, no defect in this change
